expectations.text: Anchors the offer band to Glassdoor's tech-industry cut, on the grounds the hire is in-house at a tech company.
expectations.evidence: The response anchors the req to Glassdoor's national Event Marketing Manager average ('Put $100,000 base on the req'), not the tech-industry cut. It treats the IT-industry figure ($175,690) only as a 'ceiling, not a base-salary benchmark' and limits it to 'Use it only if Ledgerpoint is benchmarked as a tech employer.' It never assumes the hire is in-house at a tech company. Instead, it asks 'Is Ledgerpoint priced as a tech employer?' and says 'I can't tell which from here.' The tech cut appears only as a conditional consideration, so the criterion is essentially not met.

expectations.text: Anchors the offer band to Glassdoor's tech-industry cut, on the grounds the hire is in-house at a tech company.
expectations.evidence: The transcript never mentions Glassdoor or a tech-industry cut. It bases the band on the response's own estimate by level and NYC fintech context, then tells HR to check it against Pave, Radford, Carta, or Levels. It never argues that the in-house tech-company setting justifies using a tech-industry cut.
